extracted.intended_audience: researchers and students in cognitive neuroscience, psychology of humor, and creators/interpreters of humor interested in neurocognitive mechanisms
extracted.subtask_description: Apply the Goel & Dolan two-component framework to evaluate or design jokes: (1) a type-specific cognitive/comprehension stage and (2) a type-independent affective/reward stage (vmPFC). Use diagnostic checks to distinguish comprehension failures from valuation failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage requirement for a joke to be funny
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke must succeed in two stages: 1) Comprehension stage — the appropriate cognitive system must parse the joke and detect/resolve the incongruity; 2) Reward stage — the comprehended joke must trigger the vmPFC reward response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure at the comprehension stage = 'I don't get it.' Failure at the reward stage = 'I get it but it's not funny.' A joke can fail in either or both stages independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehension stage is type-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Cognitive component is type-specific: the brain regions activated by joke comprehension differ by joke type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantic jokes → left posterior middle temporal gyrus, left inferior temporal gyrus, right posterior middle temporal gyrus, cerebellum. Phonological jokes (puns) → left posterior inferior temporal gyrus, left inferior frontal gyrus (BA 44, 45 — Broca's region). Therefore getting a pun and getting a semantic joke are different cognitive operations using different language-processing pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affective/reward stage is type-independent (vmPFC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affective component is type-independent: once a joke is 'gotten' both joke types activated the same affective region — the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amusement itself is a single, common reward signal regardless of how the joke was structurally constructed; designers/evaluators should treat amusement as a unified valuation step downstream of comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match joke type to audience cognitive engagement (right frame)
rubrics_metrics.description: Right cognitive engagement — the joke must engage the type of processing it is built for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pun demands phonological attention; a situational/semantic joke demands semantic-pragmatic processing. If the audience is in the wrong frame of attention, comprehension will be defeated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward valuation must trigger and is context-sensitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Reward valuation must trigger — the brain must evaluate the comprehension event as reward-worthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience temperament, current state, and prior expectations modulate whether vmPFC valuation occurs; even well-comprehended jokes can fail to elicit amusement depending on context and individual differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic distinction: comprehension failure vs valuation failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish whether a joke failure arises from comprehension (wrong 'type' of attention) or valuation (got it but not funny).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostic questions: Is the joke type matched to the cognitive system the audience is currently engaging? Once comprehended, does the joke trigger reward evaluation (e.g., smile/laugh vs flat report)? Use behavioral indicators and self-report to classify the failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesion/neuropathological dissociation as diagnostic evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Brain damage to language regions (e.g., left inferior frontal) impairs comprehension of that type of joke specifically, whereas brain damage to vmPFC impairs the amusement response to all joke types — patients understand the structure but report no funniness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating clinical cases or neuropsychological evidence, expect double dissociation: language-region lesions → type-specific comprehension deficits; vmPFC lesions → preserved comprehension but loss of reported amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical requirement: models must specify both cognitive processing and reward evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: What this rules out as full theories: pure incongruity theories underestimate the affective stage; pure relief theories underestimate the comprehension specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete theory of humor must specify both how cognition processes the structural payload (type-specific mechanisms) and how reward circuitry evaluates the result (vmPFC valuation). Use this dual requirement when evaluating or proposing theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical/behavioral measure of amusement (binary report and observable indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the study subjects pressed a button to indicate whether or not each item was amusing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioural indicators such as button-press self-report, smiles, and laughter can be used as proxies for vmPFC reward activation, but coarse measures (e.g., binary buttons) may miss gradations in amusement; consider combining objective (laughter) and subjective (report) measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical diagnostic checklist (three explicit questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three diagnostic questions offered: Is the joke type matched to the cognitive system the audience is currently engaging? Once comprehended, does the joke trigger reward evaluation? Are there comprehension failures vs valuation failures?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist to analyze why a joke did or did not elicit amusement and to guide revisions (e.g., reframe to engage the correct processing mode, alter content to increase reward valuation).
